---
title: "Models"
---

The design is tested on models that other people wrote. Each [model](README.md) comes from another framework, kept as its authors wrote it, next to the same model written in Starsim.

## The test

A model should never be easier to write without the lingua franca than with it. So each translation is held to two numbers from its original:

- **No more lines of model code**, not counting imports, comments, blank lines, and plotting.
- **No more time for a rerun**, measured on the same machine: running the same model again once it is set up, as in a parameter scan or a calibration. First-run times are shown as well, but don't count toward the mark. A first run includes setup that happens once, so a small model can take tens of milliseconds even when its reruns are much faster.

Results should also agree, within a stated tolerance. Missing any of these doesn't fail the translation: it is a gap, written up with the model for the [design](../design/index.qmd) to address. Times are not always like for like: some originals can only be timed as a whole command, and each model's notes say where that is the case.

## Where each model stands

The model names link to the [side-by-side comparison](../webapp/index.qmd), which shows the original code next to the Starsim version.

::: {.benchmark}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
import sciris as sc
build = sc.importbypath('../../scripts/build.py')
print(build.benchmark())
```
:::

## Times under each set of kernels

Starsim can run a model with its Rust, Numba, or JAX kernels. The table above gives the fastest rerun of each model, which is in bold here. Times are in seconds, and a blank means that model can't use those kernels, for example because it runs as agents.

::: {.benchmark}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
print(build.kernel_table())
```
:::

To regenerate these results, see [the benchmark](../benchmark/README.md).

## What is in each folder

Each model has the original source, where it came from and its license, reference results from running it, and its line count and run time. Next to these are the Starsim version, a script that checks it against the reference results, and notes on what was awkward or could not be expressed.

## How the models were chosen

The models are chosen to span frameworks and paradigms, and each framework's own showcase models are preferred over ones written for this project. They are brought in as a build set and held-out waves, described in [about the models](README.md).

Of the 24 frameworks [reviewed](../approaches/index.qmd), 16 have models here. The measles metapopulation model is here too, though it isn't a framework. Each of the others is left out because its models are already covered by one that is, or because a translation would test something other than how a model is written.

| Framework | Models here | Why |
|---|---|---|
| [Atomica](../approaches/atomica.md) | `hiv_dyn`, `sir` | Held-out wave 1: the strongest non-programmer specification path, in spreadsheets |
| [camdl](../approaches/camdl.md) | `sir`, `stratified` | Held-out wave 1: the closest existing thing to the target design |
| [EMULSION](../approaches/emulsion.md) | `quickstart`, `sir` | Held-out wave 1: one model run as compartments, agents, or both |
| [epidemics](../approaches/epidemics.md) | `seasonal_scenarios`, `seirv` | Added after the waves: a library of fixed models, composed into scenarios with elements |
| [EpiModel](../approaches/epimodel.md) | `hiv`, `sis-network` | Held-out wave 1: the most widely used framework in R, and the network models |
| [epipack](../approaches/epipack.md) | `siarx_tracing`, `sirs` | Added after the waves: one model run as ODEs, by Gillespie's method, and on a network, plus contact tracing |
| [epiworld](../approaches/epiworld.md) | `covid_flu`, `seirconn` | Added after the waves: several viruses and protective tools carried by the same agents |
| [Epydemix](../approaches/epydemix.md) | `covid19`, `sir_kenya` | Held-out wave 1: named in the project brief as an interconversion target |
| [epymorph](../approaches/epymorph.md) | `pei_humidity`, `sirs_centroids` | Added after the waves: disease, movement, and geography as separate parts |
| [flepiMoP](../approaches/flepimop.md) | `seir_2pop`, `vaccine_scenarios` | Held-out wave 1: models as configuration files, at production scale |
| [LASER](../approaches/laser.md) | `england_wales`, `hub_spoke_seir` | Held-out wave 1: IDM's other agent-based engine, and the speed comparison for large ABMs |
| [MEmilio](../approaches/memilio.md) | `secir`, `secir_ageres` | Held-out wave 1: the library that spans the most paradigms |
| [odin](../approaches/odin.md) | `seir_array`, `stochastic_sir_arrays` | Held-out wave 1: the best-established equations-as-code approach |
| [Pandemic Simulator](../approaches/pandemic_simulator.md) | `ebola_legrand`, `sir_reactive` | Added after the waves: a published platform of ready-made models |
| [SimInf](../approaches/siminf.md) | `sir_herds`, `sise3` | Held-out wave 1: compartments, metapopulations, and networks in one small vocabulary |
| [summer2](../approaches/summer2.md) | `seir-age-clinical`, `sir-age-location` | Held-out wave 1: the most developed answer to stratification |
| [Starsim](../approaches/starsim.md) | None | Starsim is what is being tested. Its own models (Covasim, HPVsim, STIsim, and the rest) are reviewed against v4 separately, in `tests/reviews/` |
| [MetaCast](../approaches/metacast.md) | None | No longer maintained; its metapopulation ODEs are covered by summer2, flepiMoP, and MEmilio |
| [EoN](../approaches/eon.md) | None | Network SIR and SIS, which EpiModel's network model already covers; what EoN adds is its analytic approximations, which aren't a model to translate |
| [individual](../approaches/individual.md) | None | A low-level toolkit with no disease concepts: its users write the model from scratch, so there is no showcase model of its own to translate |
| [EMOD](../approaches/emod.md) | None | A model is several large JSON files for a C++ engine, so a translation would mostly test the mapping of its parameters, not how a model is written |
| [EpiHiper](../approaches/epihiper.md) | None | Its models run on synthetic national contact networks, which aren't available to rerun here |
| [Vivarium](../approaches/vivarium.md) | None | Its models are whole microsimulations built from many components and data files, not models to translate on their own |
| [Thanzi La Onse](../approaches/tlo.md) | None | A whole health-system model, too large to translate as one model here; rebuilding it on Starsim v4 is a separate piece of work (see `admin/deferred.md`) |

Each of the frameworks with [brief notes](../approaches/notes.md) is left out too, since those notes are about one idea from each, not its models.
